title: Compact error envelopes and idempotency guidance for tool calls
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: clients and SDKs have been inconsistent when interpreting rate limit and streaming faults. Two problems surfaced in production: (1) upstream OpenAI-compatible adapters returned multiple error shapes for the same logical failure (rate limits, temporary server errors, streamed framing faults) which caused duplicate retry logic in clients, and (2) idempotency semantics for tool/function calls were under-specified, leading to two classes of duplication: repeated tool invocation when a stream reconnect occurs, and conflicting routing when idempotency keys hashed differently across ephemeral backends.

This PR introduces a compact, forward-compatible error envelope for both streaming and non-streaming paths and clarifies server-side idempotency routing and client guidance. Changes are designed for backward compatibility: legacy error shapes are mapped to the new envelope, and feature-flagged routing changes are rolled out canary-first. The description below summarizes the contract, implementation, and operational rollout plan.

Key contract (what clients should expect):
- Error envelope: {"error": {"code": string, "message": string, "meta": { optional fields: "retry_after_ms", "idempotency_conflict", "stream_frame" }}}. The envelope normalizes rate-limit hints (Retry-After -> meta.retry_after_ms) and attaches a stable code (e.g., RATE_LIMIT, TEMPORARY, STREAM_FRAME_ERROR, IDMP_CONFLICT).
- Retry semantics: 429 and transient 503/502 map to RATE_LIMIT or TEMPORARY with meta.retry_after_ms when available. Clients should prefer exponential-backoff with jitter when meta.retry_after_ms is absent; when present, respect the provided ms as a minimum backoff.
- Idempotency: servers will honor Idempotency-Key for non-streamed tool/function calls and provide deterministic routing based on a namespace hash to keep repeated attempts co-located. If a key conflicts, response uses code IDMP_CONFLICT and meta.idempotency_conflict contains a short opaque value clients can surface to users.
- Streaming reconnects: for resumed streams a client MAY reuse the same Idempotency-Key; the server will attempt best-effort deduplication but may fall back to returning STREAM_FRAME_ERROR when the resumed stream cannot be reconciled.

Implementation summary:
- openai_compat/error_mapper.py: canonicalizes legacy OpenAI shapes into the new envelope and normalizes Retry-After header into meta.retry_after_ms.
- serving/streaming: added a compact error proto and mapping helpers for streaming frame errors.
- routing: deterministic idempotency shard calculation implemented behind feature flag (infra/feature_flags/err-envelope-ff.yaml).
- SDK surfaces: python and typescript SDKs include example patterns for Idempotency-Key usage and a new helper to parse the compact envelope.
- Tests: integration tests validate deduplication behavior for repeated tool calls with identical keys and regression tests map legacy error shapes to the new envelope.

Rollout plan:
1) Canary the feature-flag behind a small percentage of traffic for 48h and monitor rate limit dashboards and idempotency conflict alerts.
2) Expand to 10% if no regressions; collect SDK telemetry.
3) Full rollout and mark as GA after one week of stability.

Compatibility notes: legacy clients that expect the older, flatter error shapes will continue to receive equivalent mappings. SDKs that adopt the new helper will get meta.retry_after_ms in ms (consistent across SDKs).

References: Linear ENG-4512 contains the audit of recent incidents; SUP-1148 collected customer reports about duplicated tool invocations.

Checklist:
- [x] Error envelope implemented and mapped in openai_compat
- [x] Deterministic idempotency routing behind FF
- [x] SDK helpers and docs updated
- [x] Integration tests added
- [x] Canary/rollout plan documented in PR description
commits_summary: Initial compact envelope prototype; map legacy errors -> envelope; add streaming proto + mapper; implement deterministic idempotency shard routing behind feature flag; add SDK parser and examples; integration tests for dedupe; docs and release notes
review_thread:
Riley Patel: Left a couple of questions about performance of the deterministic shard hash when the number of routing shards changes. Requested a comment about the intended fallback when a shard is decommissioned.
Maya Chen: Responded with design note — we include a sticky migration window; decommissioned shards trigger a re-hash with a 5m grace period and events are retried to the new shard. Added a unit test for shard migration.
Samira Gomez: Asked to clarify client guidance for when meta.retry_after_ms is missing; suggested we prefer server-side Retry-After normalization rather than exposing multiple fields.
Maya Chen: Removed redundant header exposure and updated error_mapper to always populate meta.retry_after_ms when a Retry-After header is present, converted to ms.
Anton Karpov: Approved after a small nit on naming (IDMP_CONFLICT -> IDMP_CONFLICT to keep short codes); confirmed integration tests cover resumed-stream behavior.
CI: integration tests initially failed on a flaky test (stream-resume flaky). Reran once, tests passed. Final approval and squash-merge by Anton Karpov.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash and merge. Commit message consolidates contract and implementation. Changelog: 'API: introduce compact error envelope for streaming and non-streamed tool calls; clarify idempotency routing and Retry-After semantics.'
release_notes: Introduces a normalized error envelope across the OpenAI compatibility layer and streaming paths. Clients should parse error.code and error.meta.retry_after_ms. Idempotency-Key handling for tool/function calls is now deterministic (behind feature flag) to reduce duplicate invocations during retries and stream reconnects.
rationale: Standardizing the error contract reduces client-side divergence, simplifies SDK error handling, and enables authoritative server guidance for retries. Deterministic idempotency routing reduces duplicate tool executions without requiring client changes.
fallback_policy_examples: If meta.retry_after_ms present: wait at least that many ms before retry
If meta.retry_after_ms absent and code == RATE_LIMIT: exponential backoff with initial 250ms + jitter
On IDMP_CONFLICT: surface conflict token to user and avoid automatic retry until resolved
